subject: Access controls & support access — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls discovery — FinTrust / Redwood follow-up

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can qualify next steps: 

- Scope: FinTrust is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing document summarization and internal routing. Key concern: ensuring PII never leaves our region and that support access is tightly controlled.
- PII & residency: We need confirmation of data residency guarantees and whether tokens/inputs are stored for more than 30 days by default. Do you offer per-tenant retention settings?
- RBAC & least privilege: We need a sample role matrix (admin, engineer, support, analyst) and how you enforce least-privilege across the control plane and runtime. How granular are permissions (model-level? route-level?).
- Support access / break-glass: What is Redwood's process for emergency support access? Audit trails? Just-in-time access and approvals?
- Logs & auditing: Which logs are available (request/response, redaction metadata, access logs) and retention periods?

Attached an internal system overview for context (FinTrust_System_Overview.pdf).

Next steps from our side: can your security/solutions engineer provide a one-hour technical deep dive for our engineering and security team next week?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Security, FinTrust
alex.johnson@fintrust.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls discovery — FinTrust / Redwood follow-up

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the system doc. Great working session. Below is a concise set of answers + proposed next steps. I attached a short RBAC matrix and our support-access runbook for reference (redwood-rbac-matrix.pdf; redwood-support-access-process.docx).

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Data residency & retention: Redwood supports region-specific hosting. For FinTrust we can pin all inference and storage to the US-VA region. By default, request logs and model inputs are retained for 30 days; we offer tenant-configurable retention windows (7/30/90/never) depending on the plan and contract. We can add a CL clause to lock retention at 30 days or less for enterprise contracts.

- RBAC & least-privilege: We provide role-based access with permissions at the organization, project, and route levels. Our attached matrix maps common FinTrust roles to allowed actions (view logs, run evals, manage keys, request break-glass). Role assignments can be sourced from SSO (SAML/SCIM) and we support attribute-based conditions for shorter scopes.

- Support access / break-glass: We have a documented break-glass process: support requests require a Jira ticket + 2-step approval (team on-call + customer security contact) for emergency access. All access is time-limited and logged; session recordings and a complete audit trail are retained for the contractually agreed retention window. The attached runbook includes escalation contacts and sample audit entries.

- Logs & auditing: We surface request/response metadata, redaction flags, KV-cache events (not PII), and admin actions. Full request/response payloads can be disabled per-tenant; we recommend redacting or disabling storage of raw PII fields.

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next Wed 6/23 at 10am PT with our solutions engineer (Dev) and security lead (Stephanie). Please confirm availability.
2) I’ll share our SOC2 report and a vendor questionnaire template ahead of the call.
3) If you want an initial security addendum (retention + support-access SLAs) we can produce a draft and attach it to the deal (FT-8421).

If that looks good I’ll book the meeting and share calendar invites + the two attachments.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTrust Security Team <security@fintrust.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls discovery — FinTrust / Redwood follow-up

Marissa — this looks good. Quick clarifications before we lock the deep-dive: 

- Can you confirm that break-glass approvals are customer-controlled? We prefer that FinTrust security must explicitly approve emergency support sessions (not an internal Redwood-only approval).
- For retention "never" option — is that compatible with debugging (i.e., can we enable ephemeral capture on a per-request basis for debugging with explicit consent)?

I can do 6/23 10am PT. Please send the invite and SOC2.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access controls discovery — FinTrust / Redwood follow-up

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline below and next actions at the bottom.

- Break-glass approvals: Yes — for FinTrust we’ll require explicit customer approval. Our standard enterprise workflow requires a customer security contact to approve emergency sessions; we’ll include this in the security addendum. All approvals are recorded in the audit log and surfaced in the console.

- Ephemeral debugging: Correct — you can disable persistent retention and opt into per-request ephemeral capture for debugging. Those captures are time-limited (configurable TTL) and require an explicit request (via the console or API) and an audit ticket. We can demonstrate this in the deep-dive.

Next actions:
1) Meeting scheduled: Wed, 2027-06-23 10:00am PT (invite sent).
2) I attached: redwood-rbac-matrix.pdf, redwood-support-access-process.docx and uploaded our SOC2 summary to the secure link (https://redwood.app/secure-docs/rbac-matrix).
3) I’ll send an initial security addendum draft by EOD Friday 6/18 for your review.

If you want me to include a sample SCIM mapping and example policies for FinTrust roles, say the word and I’ll add them to the packet.

Looking forward to the deep-dive —
Marissa

--
